Article Title: 'Forcibly defeated': Mayawati flags 'govt irregularities' in Rajasthan municipal polls
Article Text:
Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Bahujan Samaj Party chief Mayawati on Tuesday alleged that several candidates from her party were "forcibly defeated" in the municipal elections held in Rajasthan.In a social media post on X, Mayawati said that the BSP candidates lost by razor thin margins during recounts due to irregularities involving government machinery."In the local body elections held in Rajasthan, the BSP has also won 19 seats this time by getting its councillors elected, and many candidates have been forcibly defeated by small margins of votes during the recounting because of the irregularities of the government machinery. Otherwise, the party could have got an even better result here. For this, the party has given heartfelt congratulations and best wishes to all the small and big office-bearers and workers of the BSP," Mayawati said."However, before this, in the local body elections held in Punjab and some other states of the country, the party also got a better result than before, and they too deserve congratulations," she added.She further said that the results have increased party's hope for better performance in the upcoming assembly elections and general elections."It is hoped that in the upcoming assembly elections there and the Lok Sabha general elections in the country, all these people will ensure an even better result for their party," she said.This comes after BJP emerged as the leading party in Rajasthan’s urban local body elections.BJP secured 4,179 wards, compared with 3,613 won by Congress, and obtained clear majorities in four of the state’s 10 municipal corporations.The Congress, however, secured a majority in the Bikaner Municipal Corporation and registered a significant victory in the Jhalawar Municipal Council, which is considered a stronghold of former Rajasthan chief minister Vasundhara Raje.Out of the total votes polled across 309 civic bodies, the BJP secured 35.18 per cent (37,35,567 votes) compared to Congress's 34.24 per cent (36,35,952 votes), yielding a razor-thin winning margin of just 0.94 per cent (99,615 votes).Among the remaining contenders, the Rashtriya Loktantrik Party secured 0.94 per cent (1,00,277 votes), the Aam Aadmi Party managed to get 0.46 per cent (49,829 votes), CPM secured 0.32 per cent (34,170 votes) and the Bharat Adivasi Party recorded 0.13 per cent (14,150 votes).
Article Summary: Bahujan Samaj Party chief Mayawati alleged that several candidates from her party were "forcibly defeated" in the municipal elections held in Rajasthan. She said that the BSP candidates lost by razor thin margins during recounts due to irregularities involving government machinery.

Article Title: UP assembly elections and fight for Muslim votes: Decoding SP, Congress's Owaisi problem
Article Text:
Owaisi faces his biggest test in UP.

"I am ready to join hands. I am ready to form an alliance. Today is the time to talk. Don't cry later after the elections are over. We don't want the BJP to come to power again.” Asaduddin Owaisi, AIMIM

AIMIM’s UP plans

Bihar is AIMIM’s strongest base outside Telangana.

What makes UP challenge both interesting and difficult

Non-Yadav OBCs form the biggest bloc in UP’s caste arithmetic.

Where AIMIM matters and where it doesn't

AIMIM’s Rajasthan experiment

The BJP would be smiling either way

Akhilesh Yadav and Owaisi have long competed in appeasement politics. Now they have set aside the contest over who will be the bigger 'bhaijaan' and are looking at a 'bhaijaan collaboration'. Owaisi is effectively sending Akhilesh ji a friend request. They are two sides of the same coin Asaduddin Owaisi, AIMIM

Catch-22 for opposition parties

That was Asaduddin Owaisi 's outreach-cum-warning to Samajwadi Party chief Akhilesh Yadav in July at a rally in Moradabad while he launched AIMIM ’s campaign for the Uttar Pradesh assembly elections due early next year.Seeking alliance with opposition parties is now a part of Owaisi’s playbook to counter allegations of being a vote-cutter and the B-team of the BJP . We have seen AIMIM adopt similar strategy in other states like Maharashtra and Bihar. In both these states, it went all out to seek space in larger opposition alliances before deciding to contest on its own when its offer was rejected. Then the "rejection: became a part of Owaisi's campaign: we asked you to come in, you kept us out, so don't blame us for what happens next."So, when Owaisi reached out to Samajwadi Party in July, it was on expected lines and did not come as a surprise. But there is now a twist in the tale.Owaisi’s Uttar Pradesh plans suffered a jolt this month when one of his most trusted aides and the party’s national spokesperson Syed Asim Waqar dumped the party to join the Congress.Waqar, who rose to prominence defending the AIMIM and its politics, was a prominent voice for AIMIM in Uttar Pradesh and hence his crossing over to the Congress potentially impacts Owaisi's bid to make electoral inroads in UP.But more than his exit, it was his parting remarks that will bother Owaisi. “Being in the AIMIM for so many years, I felt that we pay lip service by stating that the BJP must be removed, but on the ground, we don't fight the BJP; we fight the Congress, the SP; we are fighting every other person who wants to remove the BJP,” Waqar said when asked about his decision to leave the AIMIM.Justifying his switch, Waqar said, “If we (AIMIM) keep fighting the opposition and do not allow it to blossom, then we are helping the BJP. I have decided that if we are true nationalists and want to remove the BJP honestly, then our objective should be to fight the BJP. If we are fighting the enemies of the BJP, then we are friends of the BJP. In reality, if someone is fighting the BJP across the country, it is Congress, Rahul Gandhi and his team. "Now, this is precisely the point which the opposition parties make against Owaisi and his AIMIM.Uttar Pradesh has been a difficult story for Owaisi. His AIMIM failed to win a single seat in the 2022 assembly elections in the state. And that makes the 2027 challenge a real test of whether the Bihar formula will work or whether Akhilesh is right to believe that AIMIM is a rival he can afford to ignore.Even while offering to join hands with Akhilesh, Owaisi chose to kick off AIMIM's 2027 campaign from Matera in Bahraich, a seat held by the Samajwadi Party. He also announced AIMIM’s candidate from the seat making his intent very clear.Owaisi questioned what SP leaders had done for the area despite getting Muslim votes, while saying AIMIM was ready for an alliance only if it was treated with 'respect' and given 'equal status'.The party has dropped enough signals to suggest that it is preparing for a much bigger push in UP in 2027. The party has also divided the state into zones and appointed regional in-charges as part of its attempt to strengthen the organisation before the election.AIMIM accepted that its performance was not up to the mark in 2022 but asserted that the party has spent the last few years trying to correct that.AIMIM's Uttar Pradesh president Shaukat Ali has said the party could contest around 200 seats if it fights alone. He has also kept the door open for a possible understanding with the BSP."Our natural alliance, if we were to forge one, would be with the BSP. Muslims and Dalits together account for nearly 40% of the vote share, enough to defeat both the SP and BJP," Ali said.The Samajwadi Party and the Congress will keep a close watch on AIMIM’s BSP outreach as it can have the potential to disrupt a lot of political calculations in the state. However, for now Mayawati has made it clear that her BSP will not forge any alliances with any party for elections.The 2027 assembly elections in UP is likely to see a very keen contest for Muslim votes. The switching of sides by Asim Waqar exposes the keen contest among the non-BJP parties for support of Muslims in the upcoming elections.The Congress, which would consider this AIMIM import as a big boost to its prospects, had contested the 2024 Lok Sabha elections in alliance with the Samajwadi Party, and, as of now, they are both part of INDIA bloc ahead of next year’s assembly elections.But this alliance has not stopped the two parties from taking measures to consolidate their individual support bases. Last month, the Samajwadi Party got a boost when the son-in-law of Congress MP from UP’s Saharanpur Imran Masood joined the party in the presence of Akhilesh Yadav. Imran Masood has been very vocal against SP and its chief Akhilesh Yadav accusing them of imposing as the ‘big-brother’ in SP-Congress alliance for the 2027 UP polls.For the SP, the Alpsankhyaks (read Muslims) form an important component of Akhilesh Yadav’s PDA outreach. In fact, his success in Uttar Pradesh till now has been largely powered by the Yadavs and the Muslims. And while, Akhilesh desperately tries to broaden his support base by reaching out to the Dalits, women and even the Pandits, he cannot make big gains without the support of Muslims.However, that does not stop the Congress from making its own outreach to the community in a bid to try and win them back. After all, for several decades the Muslims had contributed to the electoral success of the Congress. It was only with the rise of regional parties that they drifted away from the grand-old-party. So, it will naturally be happy with Asim Waqar on its side.The AIMIM, which is the third pole of Muslim politics in the state, will try to take advantage of the posturing and war of words between the two alliance partners as it tries to find its space in the state.AIMIM has shown that it can become a serious player where its support is concentrated. What it has not yet shown is that it can do the same in Uttar Pradesh, where the Samajwadi Party remains the main beneficiary of Muslim votes against the BJP.In the 2023 Telangana assembly election, the party contested nine seats and won seven, underlining how strong its hold remains in parts of the state.Bihar has been its most successful experiment outside Telangana till now. The party managed to win five seats in 2020 and repeated the number in 2025, mainly in the Seemanchal region.In Maharashtra, AIMIM has pockets of support but won just one assembly seat in 2024. In Uttar Pradesh, the challenge has been tougher. In the 2022 assembly election, AIMIM contested 96 seats but failed to win any. Its statewide vote share remained below 1%.Owaisi’s move to contest the Panchayat and Municipal body elections in Rajasthan shows the party’s intent to expand its base in states where it was not a player till now. The AIMIM chief maintains that the state needs a strong third political alternative apart from the ruling BJP and the Congress which have been the dominant players in state’s politics till now.In a bid to disturb the duoploy, Owaisi has announced that if Rashtriya Loktantrik Party chief Hanuman Beniwal emerges as a third force, the AIMIM will support him and work together to challenge both major political parties. Owaisi said, “Hanuman Beniwal and AIMIM together will make the lives of BJP and Congress leaders difficult.” He also appealed to voters to support AIMIM candidates and RLP candidates contesting elections on the party’s bottle symbol.While the Congress and the other opposition parties keep an eye on AIMIM’s political moves, the BJP perhaps would not be worried much.When Owaisi had reached out to Akhilesh, BJP wasted no time in mocking the proposal. Former BJP spokesperson Shehzad Poonawalla had then called it a 'friend request' to Akhilesh and accused both parties of vote-bank politics.For the BJP, Owaisi can be useful either way, more so in Uttar Pradesh.If AIMIM contests separately and takes away even a small number of votes from SP-Congress in close seats, the BJP may benefit. If AIMIM joins the alliance, the BJP can use Owaisi's presence to sharpen its attack on the opposition over minority appeasement.The opposition parties are reluctant to accept Owaisi’s offer to ensure that non-BJP votes, especially of the Muslims, do not split. They know that Owaisi’s offer is like a double-edged sword. Most of these opposition parties like the RJD in Bihar, Samajwadi Party in Uttar Pradesh have banked heavily on the support of Muslims for their politics. If they accept AIMIM as an ally, they fear losing the support of Muslims and this will eventually weaken their own minorities’ politics.Second, any opposition alliance with AIMIM will give the BJP a very strong weapon to engineer reverse polarisation. Since Owaisi is known for a very aggressive hardline brand of politics on issues concerning the minorities, the opposition will find it difficult to dissociate itself from the AIMIM. And this will give the BJP an opportunity to mobilise the Hindus against the opposition parties and eventually corner them.Clearly, the Samajwadi Party and the Congress have a Owaisi challenge at hand as they gear up for the 2027 challenge in Uttar Pradesh.
Article Summary: Owaisi's Uttar Pradesh plans suffered a jolt this month when one of his most trusted aides and the party’s national spokesperson Syed Asim Waqar dumped the party to join the Congress. Owaisi is effectively sending Akhilesh ji a friend request.

Article Title: Kejriwal-Sardesai Goa gambit: Attack defections, welcome rivals
Article Text:
The alliance has presented itself as a "non-BJP, non-Congress alternative".

Memory of 2017 and 2022

The 'open door' politics

The GFP complication

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

The Aam Aadmi Party and Goa Forward Party on Sunday announced a new political beginning for the state. They announced a pre-poll alliance for the upcoming 2027 assembly election named 'Goa First' and promised voters something the state has struggled to get: a mandate that actually stays intact.There was plenty of familiar political rhetoric at the launch in Panaji on Sunday. AAP national convenor Arvind Kejriwal claimed that BJP would not win a majority. "The people of Goa want a change. Goa First will form the government. We will win on our own," Kejriwal claimed.Both parties presented the alliance as a credible, "non-BJP, non-Congress alternative".In the press conference, the newly-formed alliance tried to build its political identity around a simple charge: defection.GFP chief Vijai Sardesai attacked the ruling establishment as a government of defectors. He said the BJP had not received a complete mandate in the previous elections and that even the Congress leadership could not deny the possibility of another round of defections.Kejriwal also opened up about the recent Rajya Sabha defection led by former blue-eyed boy Raghav Chadha. "It is a matter of great regret that our Rajya Sabha MPs left the party.They betrayed the party. The party sent them to the Rajya Sabha; the people did not send them," the AAP chief said.He said the AAP had never betrayed the people through its elected representatives."We believe that this is a lesson for us because such a thing has never happened in the Aam Aadmi Party before. From now onwards, before sending anyone to the Rajya Sabha, we will scrutinise the person thoroughly and ensure that he is the right person," Kejriwal said.However, after the story of 'Goa First' gets interesting, at its hard-launch itself.GFP chief Sardesai declared: "This alliance has not closed the door; it is open to the like-minded political forces. Many people have approached us, including leaders from both parties who are tired of their politics.The anti-defection pitch is not difficult to sell in Goa because voters have seen the numbers change dramatically after elections.In the 2017 assembly election, Congress emerged as the single-largest party with 17 of the 40 seats, while the BJP won 13. Yet Congress did not form the government. The BJP stitched together a coalition with regional parties and independents, with GFP chief Vijai Sardesai becoming deputy chief minister.Two years later, the picture changed again.In July 2019, 10 Congress MLAs joined BJP, taking the saffron party's strength to 27 and giving it a clear majority. The Congress, which had started the assembly term with 17 MLAs, was left with five.Then came the 2022 election.This time, BJP turned out to be the single largest party with 20 seats in the hung assembly. Congress won 11 and AAP two, while GFP won one. BJP formed the government with support from 2 independents and Maharashtrawadi Gomantak Party (MGP).Six months later, however, again eight of Congress's 11 MLAs joined BJP.Among them were former chief minister Digambar Kamat and then leader of opposition Michael Lobo. Congress was reduced to just three MLAs, while BJP's strength rose to 28.Defection runs so deep in Goa politics that, just eight months before the 2022 exodus, some Congress MLAs had gone to extraordinary lengths to prove they would stay put. They visited a temple, chapel and mosque, and signed affidavits promising not to defect. In September 2022, eight of the 11 Congress MLAs joined the BJP anyway.After years of battle in the assembly and courts, the Supreme Court in July had agreed to hear a plea challenging a decision of the Goa assembly speaker rejecting a petition by the Congress for disqualification of the eight MLAs.For Goa First, this history of defections may prove to be strong campaign material.Sardesai himself made clear that 'Goa First' is not going to be a closed club.The alliance, he said, was open to "like-minded political forces". He claimed that leaders from both major parties had already approached them because they were tired of their respective politics.Strategically, that makes perfect sense.AAP and GFP together currently have only three assembly seats. If the alliance wants to become a serious statewide force, it needs some established names and local networks. Goa's politics is intensely constituency-driven and established local faces can matter enormously.Turning away a strong BJP or Congress leader simply because that leader once belonged to the other camp could leave 'Goa First' with an admirable principle and a thin candidate list.But by welcoming such politicians, the alliance risks playing the very same game it accuses BJP of playing.However, if the leader joins before the elections, the alliance could defend it easily.There is another reason Sardesai's role makes this debate particularly interesting.GFP itself has travelled through Goa's shifting alliance landscape.In 2017, it was part of the BJP-led coalition that formed the government after Congress emerged as the largest party. By 2019, the relationship had broken down, and Sardesai became a bitter opponent of the BJP government. GFP subsequently allied with Congress for the 2022 election.It is now joining hands with AAP and positioning itself against both BJP and Congress for the 2027 elections. Thus, the positioning of the party has remained fluid.That, though, is not necessarily a contradiction, as we have seen several regional parties routinely negotiate their political space by switching alliances.The 'Goa First' alliance has now officially entered the 2027 Goa contest with defection as one of its central political themes. Yet, with its doors open to leaders from the BJP and Congress, the alliance's own composition could become part of the election narrative. The first real test of that balancing act will come with its candidate selection.
Article Summary: Aam Aadmi Party and Goa Forward Party announce a new political beginning for the state. They announced a pre-poll alliance for the 2027 assembly election named 'Goa First' Both parties presented the alliance as a credible, "non-BJP, non- Congress alternative"

Article Title: BJP stays on top, Congress gets a warning: What Rajasthan civic polls mean for 2028 assembly elections
Article Text:
Civic poll results were announced for Rajasthan wards today.

Shot in the arm for Bhajan Lal Sharma government

Mixed bag for Congress

Decisive Congress victory in Vasundhara Raje’s bastion

Boost for AAP

The 2028 challenge

NEW DELHI: The Rajasthan civic poll results have reinforced the dominance of the ruling BJP despite some setbacks, brought cheers to the AAP and the CPM, but has rung alarm bells for the Congress ahead of the 2028 assembly elections in the state.The BJP has lost some ground, but the Congress has not gained all of it. Parties like AAP and the CPM have sprung surprise in some districts at the expense of the Congress. The AAP has emerged the winner in Baran Nagar Parishad, while the CPM has gained majority in Nokha Nagar Palika.The ruling BJP led the Congress in the Rajasthan urban local body elections, winning over 4,179 wards against the opposition party's 3,613 as results for at least 10,200 wards were declared. Independents put up a strong performance across the state, winning 2,273 wards, emerging as a potentially decisive force in several urban bodies.In a post on X, PM Modi said the results reflected support for the BJP’s policies of development and good governance under the “double-engine government”.“Heartfelt thanks to the people of Rajasthan for delivering a resounding victory to the BJP in the municipal elections.This is a testament to the triumph of truth over the jhooth ki goonj (echo of lies),” PM Modi wrote.The results are a shot in the arm for chief minister Bhajan Lal Sharma. Sharma was picked up by the BJP to lead the Rajasthan government, ignoring the claims of heavyweights like Vasundhara Raje, after the party won the 2023 assembly elections against the Congress. The BJP would be happy that despite the loss of some ground, overall it has dominated across the state.The chief minister would especially be satisfied with the results as it comes in the backdrop of several controversies that had cropped up in the recent past. The NEET paper leak expose, the Karni Sena protest over UGC regulations and the CJP campaign against the state of government schools were some of the issues that had put the state government on the backfoot. But the results show that these issues may have had a limited impact on the party’s electoral prospects.Chief minister Bhajanlal Sharma thanked the voters for placing their trust in the party."Today, I express my sincere gratitude to the people of Rajasthan for the historic and magnificent victory achieved by the Bharatiya Janata Party in the state’s municipal body elections. I also thank all the party workers who dedicated their time and effort to secure this victory. I dedicate this triumph to them and to the people of Rajasthan, and offer them my congratulations and best wishes. The people of Rajasthan have endorsed the historic work accomplished in the state over the past two and a half years under the leadership of our Prime Minister Narendra Modi. They have embraced the Prime Minister’s vision of a ‘Viksit Bharat’ and a ‘Viksit Rajasthan,” he said.The CM also thanked the youth of Rajasthan for placing their trust in Prime Minister Narendra Modi and claimed that his government had, in the past two and a half years, fulfilled 78% of the pledges it made to the public.The Congress has also made significant gains in some key civic bodies, but the party should be worried about AAP and CPM entering the opposition space and making gains at its expense. The victory of AAP in Baran and CPM in Nokha should be warning bells for the Congress which has been the dominant challenger and only alternative to the ruling BJP.Reacting to the verdict, state Congress president Govind Singh Dotasra said, "When local elections happen, most votes tend to go in favour of the ruling power. This has been the trend for a long time. But this time, the BJP has been completely wiped out. In the Lok Sabha, more than 50% of their votes were there, and today they've dropped to within 34-35%.”Dostara accused the BJP of engaging in dishonest practices in the wards and delimitation.“In a major city like Jaipur, within the municipal corporation, Congress is ahead of the Bharatiya Janata Party in total votes by a margin of 10,000 votes. So, if we assess just the Jaipur Municipal Corporation, the BJP is behind Congress by 60-65 thousand votes. The vote percentage between Congress and the Bharatiya Janata Party—whenever the BJP was in power, it used to be around 9% ahead. Last time when we were in government, we were ahead by 2-2.5%. The misgovernance they've delivered, the public has shown them the mirror... In the 10 municipal corporations where the Chief Minister went, they managed a majority in only four, and that too due to dishonest delimitation; in the remaining 6, the majority is with Independents and Congress, not the Bharatiya Janata Party. This shows that this government has completely failed. Panchayat Raj elections are coming up, and in those, the Bharatiya Janata Party will face twice the debacle," the state Congress chief claimed.Dotasra also alleged that the Congress would have won around 1,500 more wards but for irregular and "unfair" delimitation of wards.He said the Congress won 542 wards reserved for Scheduled Castes, against 350 won by the BJP.In SC women-reserved wards, he said the Congress won 261 seats compared with 186 by the BJP, while in ST women-reserved wards, the Congress won 53 against the BJP's 39.Dotasra said the Congress won 37 of 80 wards in Ajmer, against 32 won by the BJP.The Congress registered a decisive victory in the Jhalawar Municipal Council, winning 18 of its 25 wards in a region considered a political stronghold of former Rajasthan chief minister and senior BJP leader Vasundhara Raje. BJP national vice president Vasundhara Raje is the sitting BJP MLA from Jhalrapatan assembly constituency of Jhalawar district. The district has a total of eight urban local bodies.The Congress also delivered a major blow to the BJP in the Pali Municipal Corporation, turning the party's traditional stronghold into a closely contested political battleground.Pali is the home district of Rajasthan BJP President Madan Rathore, who has served as the party's Pali district president several times and was a two-time MLA from Sumerpur.In a significant setback for the BJP, the Congress not only emerged as the single largest party in the 65-member Municipal Corporation but also defeated the BJP in Rathore's own ward.The AAP would be very happy with its victory in Baran. The party won 31 of the 60 wards, crossing the majority mark on its own. The Congress was a distant second with 18 wards and the BJP nine, while Independents secured two seats. The result will be a big boost for Arvind Kejriwal’s party given the fact that it has limited presence in the state.The independents have emerged as the key players in the board formation in several districts. There are several civic bodies where the BJP and the Congress will need the support of Independent councillors to ensure control. Overall, it has been a strong show by the Independents.The 2028 assembly elections are still over two years away and these results will form the basis for course corrections for all the key stakeholders. The BJP had won 115 seats with a vote share of 41.7%. The Congress claims that BJP’s Lok Sabha vote share fell 15 percentage points. This will be clear only after the final results and vote divisions are out.While the BJP will look to plug its weaknesses, the Congress will also go back to the drawing board and rework its strategy for the next state elections. In the 2023 assembly elections, the Congress had won 70 seats with a vote share of 39.58%. However, for now it has a bigger challenge at hand- to beat the BJP in wooing Independents where the party has emerged as the single largest party but could not gain majority.
Article Summary: The ruling BJP led the Congress in the Rajasthan urban local body elections, winning over 4,179 wards against the opposition party's 3,613. Independents put up a strong performance across the state, winning 2,273 wards, emerging as a potentially decisive force in several urban bodies.

Article Title: Interim EC ruling on ‘real TMC’ likely on Sept 17
Article Text:
Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: An interesting situation may be unfolding in Nandigram and Rejinagar -- the two assembly seats in West Bengal set for bypolls on Oct 6 -- with both factions of Trinamool Congress, one led by Mamata Banerjee and the other by Ritabrata Banerjee, naming own candidates while claiming to be the "real" party entitled to use its reserved 'twin flower' symbol.The Election Commission , which had heard the two factions on their claims and counter-claims on Saturday, asked them to file written replies to each other's pleas staking claim to be the "real" TMC, by Sept 16. Interestingly, Sept 16 is also the last date for filing nomination for the Nandigram and Rejinagar bypoll.Sources indicated that EC may examine the replies and come up with an interim decision on Sept 17, the day when scrutiny of nominations will take place. This may or may not be preceded by an in-person hearing. Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar is currently in Bhutan and returning by Sept 17 noon. A full commission meeting may thus have to wait till then.Given that the nominations would have been filed by the afternoon of Sept 16, with separate candidates fielded by each faction, the returning officer (RO) may need to adjudicate whether either candidates can contest under the party's reserved symbol and, if so, which one.The RO may escalate the file to the Election Commission of India through the West Bengal chief electoral officer, since EC is the authority to decide symbol disputes.Conventionally, EC freezes the party symbol in the event of an internal split and an imminent poll/bypoll, until final settlement of the dispute, and asks the rival factions to contest the poll under a new party name and symbol. The new symbol must be picked from the list of free symbols or can be of the party's own choosing.In the latest case relating to the TMC split, were the EC to issue an interim order on Sept 17 freezing the TMC symbol, the RO may allow candidates fielded by the rival groups, to contest under a different symbol. Technically, the symbols are allotted by RO to the candidates only after the last date for withdrawal of candidatures, which as per the current bypoll schedule is Sept 19.Since the rival factions would, as per the interim arrangement, need to pick new party names, there is a chance that the RO may require the rival factions' candidates to contest as independents. This is as nomination papers cannot be altered after the filing deadline.
Article Summary: Nandigram and Rejinagar, two assembly seats in West Bengal set for bypolls on Oct 6. Both factions of Trinamool Congress, one led by Mamata Banerjee, naming own candidates. Claim to be the "real" party entitled to use its reserved 'twin flower' symbol.

Article Title: Indian travel vlogger claims ‘arrest’ by Afghan ‘Mujahideen’, seeks help
Article Text:

NEW DELHI: A popular Indian travel vlogger from Kerala, who has been travelling in Afghanistan and posting videos from the country, on Monday claimed that she had been "arrested" by the "Mujahideen" in Bamyan and appealed for help in contacting the Indian embassy.In a post on her Facebook page, the vlogger, "Backpacker Arunima", shared what she described as a translation of an official communication from local authorities, stating that she had been arrested by the Mujahideen in Afghanistan."You were arrested by Mujahideen just now because you do not have an official letter," the translated message read."Backpacker Arunima" also appealed for assistance in reaching the Indian embassy."If you anyone know Indian embassy please contact," she wrote.The veracity of the post could not be independently ascertained, and there was no immediate response from the Ministry of External Affairs.The post offered no further details about the circumstances of her alleged arrest or identified those who had detained her.Arunima has been travelling across Afghanistan and has shared several videos from the country on her social media accounts. She has more than 1.2 million followers on Instagram and 2.39 lakh on Facebook, while her YouTube channel has over 7.3 lakh subscribers.According to her social media profiles, she has spent the past six years hitchhiking through remote routes and documenting "rare and risky" regions.
Article Summary: 'Backpacker Arunima' has been travelling across Afghanistan and has shared several videos from the country on her social media accounts. She has more than 1.2 million followers on Instagram and 2.39 lakh on Facebook, while her YouTube channel has over 7.3 lakh subscribers.

Article Title: Inspiring story of the day: “Having a dad with a big name doesn’t do the work for you” - How Trinity Rodman rose above Dennis Rodman’s shadow, lived in motels, and built her own soccer legacy
Article Text:
Inspiring story of the day: “Having a dad with a big name doesn’t do the work for you” - How Trinity Rodman rose above Dennis Rodman’s shadow, lived in motels, and built her own soccer legacy

How did Trinity Rodman live in a car despite being Dennis Rodman’s daughter

Call Her Daddy

What did Trinity Rodman say about her relationship with Dennis Rodman

Why does Trinity Rodman call Michelle Moyer her role model?

How did Trinity Rodman turn a difficult childhood into a soccer career

Why is Trinity Rodman’s story inspiring beyond soccer

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Trinity Rodman has built a soccer career that now stands on its own. The Washington Spirit star is a 2024 Olympic gold medalist, a 2021 NWSL champion and, as of January 2026, the highest-paid player in NWSL history. But her childhood looked very different from what many people expected from the daughter of NBA legend Dennis Rodman . Trinity and her brother DJ once lived with their mother, Michelle Moyer, in a Ford Expedition and cheap motels in Newport Beach. Through those difficult years, Michelle kept life feeling normal for her children. That bond helped shape Trinity into the player she is today.Having a famous father did not mean Trinity Rodman grew up with an easy life. After Dennis Rodman and Michelle Moyer separated, Trinity, her brother DJ and their mother faced serious money problems. For a period, they moved between a Ford Expedition and motels when Michelle could afford a room.The situation was especially strange because they were living in Newport Beach, where Trinity went to a wealthy school. She has spoken about seeing classmates arrive in expensive cars while her own family was trying to work out where they would stay.On, Trinity explained just how unusual those years were:“We had a Ford Expedition and we lived in that for a little bit. Mind you, in Newport Beach… So imagine living in a car going to a rich school when everybody else is in Rolls-Royces and Range Rovers. But my mom tried to make every situation seem smoother than it actually was. For me and DJ, it was never embarrassing because we had each other and we had our mom.”For Trinity and DJ, however, those memories were not only painful. Their mother tried hard to make sure they still had happy childhood moments. At motels, they could eat breakfast, use the pool and spend time together before school. That helped the children see their family life differently from how an outsider might have seen it.Trinity’s relationship with Dennis Rodman has remained one of the most talked-about parts of her story, but it has also been one of the most painful. She has said that her father was often absent while she was growing up and that there were long periods when they had little contact.That distance became impossible to ignore as Trinity began making a name for herself in soccer. Instead of being known only as an athlete, she was repeatedly asked about being Dennis Rodman’s daughter.She later spoke openly about how difficult that connection could feel:“He’s a person. He’s not a dad. Maybe by blood, but nothing else… Hearing his voice is painful because it’s missing him mixed with the fact that he’s an alcoholic. I answer the phone now for my conscience, but it took me a long time to realize that having a dad with a big name doesn’t do the work for you. I had to build everything myself.”Dennis has also publicly admitted that he was not the father he wanted to be. At his Basketball Hall of Fame induction, he said he wished he had been a better father.For Trinity, though, her own career could not depend on her father’s reputation. Her speed, finishing, attacking ability and work on the field became the things that made people remember her.If Dennis Rodman gave Trinity a famous last name, Michelle Moyer gave her the support that helped her grow into a professional athlete. Michelle raised Trinity and DJ largely as a single mother and remained closely involved in Trinity’s soccer journey.The Guardian reported in 2021 that Trinity saw her mother as her main support system. That feeling has remained central to how she talks about her childhood and her success.Trinity Rodman put it simply:“My mom wasn’t in the NBA, but she’s my role model. She is my world, my rock, and my right hand. She’s the strongest person I know. People always say, ‘Oh, you get your athleticism from your dad,’ but my work ethic, my heart, my grit, and the woman I am today-that’s 100% my mom.”That is an important part of Trinity Rodman’s story because her biggest influence was not another famous athlete. It was the person who was there when money was tight, when the family had nowhere stable to stay and when Trinity was still only a young girl trying to understand her world.Trinity’s soccer career moved quickly once she reached the professional level. She entered the NWSL with the Washington Spirit in 2021 and became the youngest player ever selected in the league’s draft at the time. She went on to win the NWSL Rookie of the Year award and helped the Spirit win the league championship that same year.Her rise continued with the U.S. women’s national team. She became an important attacking player for the USWNT and was part of the squad that won Olympic gold at the 2024 Paris Games.The success also changed the way her name was viewed. Instead of being introduced mainly as Dennis Rodman’s daughter, Trinity became a major soccer star in her own right.In January 2026, she reached another major point in her career when she re-signed with the Washington Spirit on a deal worth more than $2 million per year. The agreement made her the highest-paid player in NWSL history.That achievement says a lot about how far she has come. The girl who once went to school after sleeping in a car is now one of the biggest names in American women’s soccer.Trinity Rodman’s story is not simply about becoming famous despite having a difficult childhood. It is about how she chose to define herself.She could have spent her career being introduced through her father’s name. Instead, she has built an identity around her own performances and the people who stood beside her. Her mother remained a constant presence, while soccer gave Trinity a place where her effort could speak for itself.Her journey also explains why the success means more than trophies and contracts. The Olympic gold medal, NWSL championship and record-breaking deal are major achievements, but they came after years of work that had little to do with her father’s fame.Trinity has been clear about that point herself: a famous parent can give someone a name, but it cannot do the training, handle the pressure or play the game for them.For Trinity Rodman, the most important part of her legacy may be that she did not allow her father’s story to become her own. She took the difficult parts of her childhood, held on to the support her mother gave her and built a career that now belongs completely to her.
Article Summary: Trinity Rodman has built a soccer career that now stands on its own. The Washington Spirit star is a 2024 Olympic gold medalist, a 2021 NWSL champion and, as of January 2026, the highest-paid player in NWSL history. But her childhood looked very different from what many people expected from the daughter of NBA legend Dennis Rodman.

Article Title: Welles Crowther’s inspiring 9/11 story: How a former Boston College lacrosse player became the man in the red bandana
Article Text:
Welles Crowther (Credit: Welles Remy Crowther Charitable Trust)

Welles Crowther and the red bandana that became his legacy

The man in the red bandana became a 9/11 hero

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Twenty-five years after September 11, 2001, the story of Welles Crowther still carries a powerful message about courage. A former Boston College lacrosse player working in the World Trade Center, Crowther chose to help others when thousands were trying to escape. His red bandana became a symbol of hope for survivors and a lasting reminder of one man’s extraordinary decision to put strangers before himself.Crowther had carried a red bandana since childhood. His father gave it to him when he was six, and it eventually became part of his identity.Long before the tragedy, Crowther had already shown an interest in helping others. At 16, he signed up to become a junior firefighter. His father, Jefferson Crowther, later remembered a conversation that showed where his son's ambitions were heading.“Welles called me one day and said, ‘I think I want to change my career,’ ” his father, Jefferson Crowther, recalled in a 2019 ESPN feature, The Man in the Red Bandana. “He said, ‘I think I want to be a New York City firefighter.’ ”Instead, Crowther began a career in finance. In 1999, he joined an equity firm and worked on the 104th floor of the South Tower.On September 11, 2001, his professional life became secondary to something far more urgent.After the attacks, survivors recalled a young man moving through the smoke and confusion, helping injured people and directing them toward safety. They did not know his name. They remembered the red bandana covering his face.One survivor, Ling Young, later described the moment Crowther appeared.“A young man come out of nowhere. This man’s voice said, ‘I found the stairs, follow me and only help the ones you can help.’ It was the way he said it, we just got up and we followed.”Crowther helped people reach a functioning stairwell and guided them toward firefighters. But rather than leaving with those he had helped, he went back upstairs.That decision became the defining part of his story.Crowther continued moving through the South Tower, helping people escape and providing assistance to those who were injured. Judy Wein was among those he helped, according to accounts later shared by her husband, Gerry.“She had just come out of surgery,” Gerry recalled of the days after the terrorist attack. “At that point, she could hardly speak but she wanted to tell me what happened. She said a young man appeared out of nowhere. She watched as he went around helping people, putting out fires and administering aid to the injured,” he recalled.For Crowther’s parents, the mystery surrounding their son’s final hours lasted for months. They eventually learned about the unidentified rescuer described by survivors. When they showed photographs of Crowther, survivors recognized him as the man who had guided them.Crowther’s body was later found in the lobby of the South Tower alongside firefighters. Accounts credit him with helping as many as 12 people survive the attacks.His actions also created a legacy that reached far beyond New York.In 2006, Crowther was posthumously named a New York City firefighter. That same year, his Boston College teammate Tyler Jewell honored him while competing in the Winter Olympics.“For me, the red bandana symbolizes everything I want to be and everything Welles was,” Jewell said in The Man in the Red Bandana. “Strength, honor, courage — he’s a true hero.”The red bandana has since become closely associated with Crowther’s memory at Boston College. The school’s annual Red Bandanna Game keeps his story alive for a new generation of students and athletes.The tradition is more than a tribute to a former lacrosse player. It reflects the values that Crowther displayed when his own safety was at stake.His story remains striking because he did not know the people he helped. He had no guarantee that anyone would remember his name. He simply saw people who needed help and acted.That is why Welles Crowther’s legacy has endured. The red bandana is easy to remember, but the choice behind it is what made him a hero.
Article Summary: Welles Crowther was a former Boston College lacrosse player. He worked on the 104th floor of the South Tower of the World Trade Center. Crowther helped people reach a functioning stairwell and guided them to firefighters. He was found dead in the lobby of the North Tower.

Article Title: Rafael Nadal bought 7,000-sq-metre Mallorca clifftop plot for €4 million after €5.7 million asking price, then spent 3 years rebuilding it as his family home
Article Text:
Rafael Nadal bought 7,000-sq-metre Mallorca clifftop plot for €4 million after €5.7 million asking price, then spent 3 years rebuilding it as his family home

How did Rafael Nadal buy the Porto Cristo property for €4 million

What did Rafael Nadal build on the 7,000-square-metre site

When was Rafael Nadal’s Mallorca home finally completed

Why is Porto Cristo important to Rafael Nadal and Maria Francisca Perelló

What other property does Rafael Nadal own outside Mallorca

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Rafael Nadal spent €4 million on a 7,000-square-metre coastal property in Porto Cristo, Mallorca, after it was originally listed for €5.7 million. The 22-time Grand Slam champion bought the land and an old Majorcan stone house in 2013, then later replaced the original buildings with a modern family home. The property sits above Porto Cristo’s harbour and has wide views of the Mediterranean. Construction on the new home began after Nadal married Maria Francisca Perelló in 2019 and was completed in 2023. Today, the estate remains closely tied to Nadal’s life in Mallorca.The property Rafael Nadal bought in 2013 was not a new luxury villa. It included a traditional Majorcan stone chalet and other buildings spread across about 7,000 square metres of land on the coast of Porto Cristo. The estate had belonged to the heirs of people linked to the development of the nearby Caves of Drach, one of Mallorca’s best-known attractions.The asking price was €5.7 million, but Nadal eventually agreed to pay €4 million. That meant he secured the property for about €1.7 million less than the original asking price.The location was also important. Porto Cristo is on Mallorca’s eastern coast and is close to Manacor, where Nadal was born and where his tennis academy is based.The property gave him a private home near his family and the part of the island that has remained central to his life.The purchase was reported by the Majorca Daily Bulletin in 2020, when the property was still being rebuilt. At the time, the publication described the site as a 7,000-square-metre coastal estate with the old stone chalet still on it.Nadal did not simply update the old house. The original buildings were taken down as part of a much bigger project, and a new home was designed for the family.Mallorcan architect Tomeu Esteva worked on the project. The finished property has a modern look but still fits its coastal setting. Large windows bring the sea views into the main living areas, while stone and other natural materials keep the design connected to Mallorca.The home includes large outdoor areas, terraces and an infinity pool facing the harbour. The layout also gives the family plenty of private space away from the public areas of Porto Cristo.Architectural Digest reported that the home sits on a 1.7-acre plot overlooking the port and described it as Nadal’s main home in Mallorca. The publication also noted that Esteva designed the modern villa after the original property was acquired by Nadal.The size of the land is one of the biggest features of the estate. Instead of building a home that dominates the site, the project uses the coastal position, views and outdoor space as major parts of the property.The rebuild took several years. Work began after Nadal and Maria Francisca Perelló married in October 2019, but the project was not finished quickly.Building a large home on a coastal site involved a long planning and construction process. By 2023, the work was finally close to completion, and the family began using the property as their home.In September 2023, Nadal himself gave followers a glimpse of the finished property. He shared a photograph from the infinity pool, with Porto Cristo’s harbour visible behind him, and wrote, “Working,” alongside Bon Jovi’s “It’s My Life.”The Majorca Daily Bulletin reported at the time that the work had been completed at the start of that summer. It also noted that the property’s interconnected buildings sit on the 7,000-square-metre plot and that Nadal could see his catamaran, Great White, from the home.That timing also made the house especially significant in Nadal’s life. He retired from professional tennis in November 2024 after a career that included 22 Grand Slam singles titles. The Porto Cristo home was therefore already in place as he moved into life away from the regular demands of the ATP Tour.For Nadal, the property is not simply another expensive home. Its location keeps him close to Manacor, the town where he grew up and where his family has deep roots.Nadal’s parents live nearby, while the Rafa Nadal Academy is also in Manacor. The academy opened in 2016 and has become an important part of his work away from the professional tour.The Porto Cristo property also puts Nadal close to the sea. His 80-foot Sunreef Power catamaran, Great White, was delivered in 2020. Sunreef Yachts confirmed that Nadal commissioned the boat and designed it with family use and time on the water in mind.That connection between the house and the sea has been visible in photographs Nadal has shared from the property. The home overlooks the harbour, while the yacht is kept nearby, making it easy for Nadal and his family to spend time on the water.The estate is also the family home for Nadal, Perelló and their children. Their first son, Rafael, was born in October 2022, while their second son, Miquel, was born in August 2025.The Porto Cristo estate is not Nadal’s only major property. He has also owned a home in the Dominican Republic, where he bought a villa in the Playa Nueva Romana resort.His property holdings have also expanded to Madrid. In March 2024, the Majorca Daily Bulletin reported that Nadal had bought a luxury home in the Spanish capital. The residence was described as a 280-square-metre property with four bedrooms and five bathrooms, along with shared facilities including a spa and gym.Nadal has also moved into the hospitality business. He partnered with Meliá Hotels International to launch the ZEL hotel brand, which combines the Nadal name with a Mediterranean lifestyle theme.Still, Porto Cristo has a different role from those investments. The Madrid home serves a major city, the Dominican Republic property is a holiday retreat and the ZEL project is a business venture. The Mallorca estate is tied directly to Nadal’s family life and his connection to the island where his tennis story began.The €4 million purchase therefore became much more than a property deal. Nadal bought a large piece of the Mallorca coast at a significant discount to its original asking price, rebuilt it over several years and turned it into a private home overlooking Porto Cristo. With his professional career now over, the property gives him a permanent base close to Manacor, his family and the sea.
Article Summary: Rafael Nadal spent €4 million on a 7,000-square-metre coastal property in Porto Cristo, Mallorca, after it was originally listed for €5.7 million. The 22-time Grand Slam champion bought the land and an old Majorcan stone house in 2013, then later replaced the original buildings with a modern family home. Construction on the new home began after Nadal married Maria Francisca Perelló in 2019 and was completed in 2023.

Instead of simply trying to push through them, Bündchen eventually began looking at what was happening beneath the surface.She recently reflected on that period during an appearance on the i-D podcast. Her description was not simply about anxiety. It was about losing touch with herself and then slowly finding her way back.“I feel like there is many deaths and rebirths in my life,” she shared on the i-D podcast, answering a fan's question. “I think when you're 46, you definitely have gone through a few of those, but I would say one of the most intense ones for me was when I had panic attacks, and I was dealing with it in my early 20s for about two years.I think I was living so much outside of myself, almost detached and trying to be a pleaser.“It's when I really had to dive deep, and I discovered who I was, and I realized that my body was my temple and I could be the director of my own movie, that I could create my life, and that was very powerful moment. So I'm very grateful. That's why I say, ‘What doesn't kill you makes you stronger.'”That period became a foundation for Bündchen's approach to wellness. She later made changes to her diet and daily habits, placing greater importance on health rather than simply maintaining the image expected of her.Bündchen's personal journey took another major turn through her marriage to Tom Brady. The couple married in 2009 and became parents to Benjamin and Vivian. Their relationship brought family life into an already demanding world of professional sports and modelling.Their divorce in 2022 marked another difficult transition. Brady later acknowledged how deeply the separation affected him, including its impact on his football career.“It was a challenge,” Brady told FOX News. “It just took a lot out of me in terms of my ability to continue to play.”Bündchen also spoke about the emotional weight of seeing a future she had imagined take a different path.“It's tough because you imagine your life was going to be a certain way, and you did everything you could, you know?” she told Vanity Fair.Rather than allowing those experiences to define her, Bündchen continued building a life around health and self-awareness. Her 2024 book,, further explored those ideas and encouraged readers to think differently about their relationship with food and wellbeing.“This is my temple,” Bündchen said on GMA. “I only get one, so I how can I nourish it? And how can I love it? If it's not nourishing me, then I'm not going to eat it. I think that's the number one thing. Making a commitment to your health.”For Bündchen, the biggest lesson from those difficult chapters appears to be ownership. Fame, marriage and major life changes brought challenges she could not always control. But she found a way to regain control over how she cared for herself and what came next.
Article Summary: Gisele Bündchen has opened up about the panic attacks she faced in her early 20s. She described the experience as a turning point that changed how she viewed her body, choices and future. Years later, after her marriage to Tom Brady ended, those lessons continued to shape the way she approached life and wellness.

Article Title: How Kenneth Walker is quietly becoming the most important player on the Chiefs' roster
Article Text:
Kenneth Walker is one of the most important Chiefs players at present (Getty Images)

Why is Kenneth Walker the Chiefs' most important player right now?

What makes Kenneth Walker different from every other Chief running back in recent memory?

How does Walker's role with the Chiefs compare to his time in Seattle?

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Kenneth Walker had 14 carries for 89 yards in the first half of Kansas City's Week 1 matchup against the Denver Broncos. He set up a Mahomes touchdown on the opening drive. Then added two receptions. Then a 28-yard carry that was the longest play of the game. For a Chiefs team returning from a 6-11 collapse and a quarterback still finding his footing after ACL surgery, Walker did not just contribute. He carried the offense. And that was only the first half.Patrick Mahomes is the name on the marquee, but Walker is the reason this offense functions. That sounds like an overstatement. It isn't. When the Chiefs signed Walker to a three-year deal worth up to $45 million in March, the move was framed as a backfield upgrade. What it actually was, was a structural fix.Kansas City has not had a 1,000-yard rusher since Mahomes took over as the starting quarterback. That is a stunning gap for a team that won multiple Super Bowls. The passing game covered it up for years. Then Mahomes tore his ACL in Week 15 of 2025, the Chiefs went 6-11, and suddenly the absence of a credible ground game was impossible to ignore.Walker is also reviving something that had gone dormant in Andy Reid's offense for years: the screen game.During Reid's early tenure with Kansas City, Jamaal Charles gave him the personnel to run one of the most dangerous screen attacks in the NFL. That element has been absent since. Walker, who told Kay Adams he had been working directly with Mahomes to build passing game chemistry, averaged fewer than 40 catches per season in Seattle. That number is expected to jump considerably here.According to Jesse Newell of The Athletic, Reid opened up his screen-game playbook in training camp and Walker was the primary target, flashing strong receiving skills and even occasional one-handed catches.Walker forced 77 missed tackles across the 2025 regular season and playoffs, trailing only Bijan Robinson over that span, while earning a 91.4 PFF grade. He has improved his overall PFF grade every single season of his career. That kind of consistency is rare. So is his running style.At his July training camp press conference, Walker explained how patience and explosiveness coexist in his game. "I would just believe over the years running the ball since growing up, and just working with my pops, just seeing the defense is I believe that's how I really learned how to be patient or, you know, explosive. It just depends on what the play is, honestly," Walker said. "I feel like that helps the O-Line...whatever they need me to do, that's what I'm gonna do. "The Chiefs have no real competition for passing-down work behind Walker. After waiving Emari Demercado, the remaining backs on the roster are Emmett Johnson, a Day 3 rookie, and Brashard Smith, a gadget player without the size to reliably block. The result is a roster built around giving Walker every snap they can justify.The Chiefs internally view Walker as a three-down back. That is not a label Kansas City has applied to a running back in a long time.This is where context matters. Walker spent four years in Seattle largely underused, splitting touches with Zach Charbonnet and never fully earning a bell-cow role until Charbonnet's knee injury forced the Seahawks' hand late in the 2025 season. His usage in Seattle prior to that injury was likely a team preference rather than any reflection on Walker himself.In Super Bowl LX, Walker ran for 135 yards on 27 carries with two receiving touchdowns as Seattle defeated New England 29-13. He became the first running back to win Super Bowl MVP since Terrell Davis did it for Denver in Super Bowl XXXII.Kansas City did not sign a complementary piece. They signed a player whose ceiling had been artificially suppressed for years. The difference is real. In Seattle, Walker worked within a system that never fully committed to him.In Kansas City, the system is being designed around what he does.Week 1 against Denver was one data point. But the role, the contract, the scheme, and the 28-yard burst that stopped a stadium cold in the first half all point toward the same thing. Walker is not a piece of the Chiefs' rebuild. He is the foundation of it.
Article Summary: Kenneth Walker had 14 carries for 89 yards in the first half of Kansas City's Week 1 matchup against the Denver Broncos. The Chiefs signed Walker to a three- year deal worth up to $45 million in March. Walker is reviving something that had gone dormant in Andy Reid's offense for years.

Article Title: NBA trade news: Clippers finally bid farewell to $375.8 million 6-foot-6 forward to Raptors after controversial delay
Article Text:
Clippers traded Kawhi Leonard to the Raptors. Image via: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect

Category Details Player Kawhi Leonard Former Team Los Angeles Clippers New Team Toronto Raptors Contract Status Final year of three-year, $103 million deal signed in 2019; extension expected with Raptors Clippers Receive Brandon Ingram, Gradey Dick, 2031 and 2033 unprotected first-round picks, 2027 first-round pick swap, 2030 and 2033 second-round picks Original Agreement June 30 League Approval Monday

Kawhi Leonard returns to Raptors from Clippers

Kawhi Leonard's Clippers-Raptors trade details

Why was Kawhi Leonard's Clippers-Raptors trade delayed?

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

It has been a while but the wait is over. Kawhi Leonard is in the Toronto Raptors again, and the trade reuniting him with the franchise he led to a championship in 2019 is no longer hypothetical. The Raptors and Clippers received league approval Monday to finalize the deal both sides shook hands on back in late June, ending a stretch where an already-completed trade sat frozen because of an active NBA investigation.Nothing about the trade package changed in the two and a half months it spent in limbo. The Clippers still get Brandon Ingram, Gradey Dick and a stack of draft compensation, and the Raptors still get their franchise cornerstone back. What changed is the context: the NBA's probe into how the Clippers paid Leonard is now closed, complete with penalties that reshaped the roster math on both sides.Kawhi Leonard's return closes a loop that started when he left Toronto for the Clippers after that 2019 title run, still the only championship of his career.Raptors general manager Bobby Webster called it a statement move for a franchise trying to get back into contention, saying Leonard's "impact on our organization, our city and our country is undeniable."Leonard framed the moment as a reset after a turbulent offseason, saying he's "focused on what I can control, closing this chapter." At 35, he's coming off the best statistical season of his career, a career-high 27.9 points across 65 games for the Clippers last year, along with 6.4 rebounds and 3.6 assists.The trade framework has been the same from what the two sides agreed in June. Toronto sends Leonard west and gets back a package built almost entirely on draft capital: two unprotected first-round picks in 2031 and 2033, a first-round pick swap in 2027, and second-round picks in 2030 and 2033.The Clippers get two rotation pieces in return. Ingram, extended to a three-year, $120 million deal shortly after Toronto acquired him, averaged 21.5 points, 4.8 rebounds and 3.7 assists last season. Dick, the Raptors' 2023 first-round pick, saw his role shrink, with his scoring dropping to 6.0 points per game on 30% 3-point shooting.The agreement sat frozen because the NBA was investigating whether the Clippers circumvented the salary cap when they signed Leonard to that three-year, $103 million deal in July 2019, reportedly including a no-show job worth $28 million. Both franchises agreed not to finalize the trade until the league closed its probe. The findings landed hard: Ballmer drew a one-year suspension and a $30 million fine, and the team forfeited five first-round picks. Leonard himself was fined $700,000, though the league didn't suspend him or void his contract. As for his fortune, Leonard is estimated to have earned approximately $375.8 million in NBA salary through the end of the 2026-27 season.Ballmer has already said he won't challenge the punishment. For Leonard, the next milestone is a contract extension with Toronto, something the Clippers weren't willing to offer. Toronto hosts the Clippers in a preseason game in Vancouver on Oct. 10, the Raptors visit Los Angeles on Nov. 2, and the Clippers head to Toronto on Jan. 1.
Article Summary: Kawhi Leonard was traded to the Toronto Raptors from the Los Angeles Clippers. The Raptors and Clippers received league approval Monday to finalize the deal. The Clippers still get Brandon Ingram, Gradey Dick and a stack of draft compensation. The NBA's probe into how the Clippers paid Leonard is now closed.

Article Title: What did Peyton Manning say after Bo Nix’s costly interception? Denver Broncos suffer heartbreaking 31-10 loss to Patrick Mahomes and the Kansas City Chiefs
Article Text:
What did Peyton Manning say after Bo Nix’s costly interception? (Getty Images)

Peyton Manning breaks down the interception that gave Chiefs an early opening

Bo Nix quickly answered Peyton Manning’s concern

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Bo Nix’s return to the Denver Broncos lineup could hardly have started worse. On Monday, Nix threw an interception on Denver’s first passing attempt against the Kansas City Chiefs, leaving Peyton Manning visibly stunned during the ManningCast.The Hall of Fame quarterback watched Nix’s comeback from the ManningCast booth with his brother Eli Manning. Nix had not played a regular-season game since fracturing his ankle in Denver’s AFC Divisional Round win over Buffalo last season, and his first series at Arrowhead Stadium quickly gave Manning something to react to.The problem started before Nix even got a chance to settle into the game. He took a sack on Denver’s opening play, ran on the second play and then dropped back on third down looking for Courtland Sutton.Chiefs rookie Mansoor Delane jumped the route and intercepted Nix, giving Kansas City possession at the Denver 46-yard line. Manning immediately reacted during the ManningCast alternate broadcast on ESPN2.“Oh, no, no, no, no,” Manning said during the Sept. 14 ManningCast while reacting to the interception.The Mannings then went through the coverage. Peyton initially read the play as a two-man look, while Eli pointed out that Kansas City actually had a single-high safety.Eli felt Delane guessed on the route and nearly stumbled into the interception.Peyton then explained why he viewed the play as a fortunate break for the rookie cornerback.“He’s lucky he ran the in route, because the trail technique without a safety help over the top, if you go deep, it’s going to be wide open,” Manning said during the ManningCast. “He really lucks out on that play.”That gave the Chiefs a chance to turn Nix’s mistake into points, and they did exactly that. Kenneth Walker III carried the ball seven times for 32 yards on the drive before Patrick Mahomes finished it with a 15-yard touchdown run.Nix did not let the interception define his return. Denver’s next possession looked completely different, with the quarterback completing all five of his passes for 55 yards and ending the drive with a 19-yard touchdown pass to tight end Evan Engram. The score tied the game at 7-7.Manning acknowledged the response while continuing to point out how fortunate Delane had been on the earlier play. “He should have guessed right,” Manning said during the ManningCast. “Pretty good start to his career, Eli.”Nix’s quick response offered Denver an early lift, but the Broncos could not keep pace with Kansas City. The Chiefs eventually pulled away for a 31-10 victory at Arrowhead Stadium on September 14.The result also flipped the script from 2025. Denver had swept Kansas City in both meetings last season and won the AFC West for the first time in a decade. This time, Mahomes and the Chiefs opened the new season with a convincing win while Nix’s comeback began with one interception that had Peyton Manning shaking his head.
Article Summary: Bo Nix threw an interception on Denver’s first passing attempt against the Kansas City Chiefs. Peyton Manning immediately reacted during the ManningCast alternate broadcast on ESPN2. The Chiefs eventually pulled away for a 31-10 victory at Arrowhead Stadium on September 14.
